added_claim_errors: “我能不能以灵活就业身份补3–9月”: wrong months. She left in March and had paid for March, so the gap is April to October 2026.
“另加大病、长护险几十元”: per the key, these premiums come out of the money credited to the personal account during back-payment, not as extra cash.
“花3,300元买7个月年限，对你没有实际收益”: overstated. The 7 months count toward the 10-year and 20-year requirements and would avoid the retirement lump sum (743.60元/月, 5,205.20元 for 7 months) if she ends up short.

“连续缴费年限：断缴3个月以上会重新计算”: presents recalculated continuous years as a concept in Hangzhou employee insurance. Per the key, “重新计算” appears only in the resident major-illness continuous-enrolment reward. Unverifiable.
“省内换工作不用转移”: other Zhejiang cities are outside the key; unverifiable.
“正常上班到退休只会超过，不会不够”: depends on her age, which the answer does not know; stated as certain.

“另扣大病保险（48元/年）、长护险（45元/年）…约54元；合计约3,370元”: per the key, these premiums are deducted from the money credited to the personal account, not paid as extra cash. The 45元/年 long-term-care figure is also unverifiable.
Quotes the rule as “参保缴费次次月”. The key's wording is “自恢复缴费月起的第三个自然月”. The meaning matches, but the quoted text is unverifiable.
“按现行口径，也不会缩短重新参保后的等待期”: stated as settled. The key marks whether back-payment waives the waiting period as unverified.
“实际净支出会略低于3,370元”: muddled. Money credited to the personal account does not lower what she pays at the counter.
Same “连续缴费年限…重新计算” framing for employee insurance; per the key, “重新计算” appears only in the resident major-illness reward. Unverifiable.

reasons: Both answers open by rejecting the claim that the 8 years are wiped out, and both give January 2027 as the date reimbursement resumes, with 473.67元/月 as the back-payment rate. B covers every key point with the exact figures: 3,315.69元 for 7 months, the 24-month and 144-month gaps, the 2026-12-31 deadline, the eligibility rules, that the new employer cannot back-pay, and the retirement lump sum of 743.60元/月 (5,205元), along with the assumptions these rest on. A is tighter. But it gets the months wrong (3–9月 instead of 4–10月), skips the new-employer point and the cost of not back-paying, and never works out the 24-month gap to 10 years in Hangzhou. Both wrongly add the major-illness and long-term-care premiums as extra cash. B is too long and states one unverified point as fact (back-payment does not shorten the waiting period), but it is much more complete and actionable.
